extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, policymakers, and practitioners researching U.S. Inspector General law
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes statutory requirements, duties, appointment and independence provisions created by the Inspector General Act of 1978 and later amendments (notably the 2008 Reform Act and the 2022 Securing Inspector General Independence Act). Useful for understanding legal standards governing U.S. Inspectors General and OIG offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General appointment qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: "There shall be at the head of each Office an Inspector General who shall be appointed by the President, without regard to political affiliation and solely on the basis of integrity and demonstrated ability in accounting, auditing, financial analysis, law, management analysis, public administration, or investigations." (5 U.S.C. § 403 / IG Act, sec. 3(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies presidential appointment; appointment must be nonpartisan and competency-based in enumerated professional fields. Implies evaluative standards for candidate selection (integrity and demonstrated ability in listed disciplines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General reporting relationship and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each Inspector General shall report to and be under the general supervision of the head of the establishment involved or, to the extent such authority is delegated, the officer next in rank below such head, but shall not report to, or be subject to supervision by, any other officer of such establishment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a limited reporting chain to ensure operational independence; further provides that "Neither the head of the establishment nor the officer next in rank below such head shall prevent or prohibit the Inspector General from initiating, carrying out, or completing any audit or investigation, or from issuing any subpoena during the course of any audit or investigation." These clauses function as anti-interference protections for audits/investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core duties and authorities of Inspectors General
rubrics_metrics.description: IGs were given authority to review the internal documents of their departments or offices and responsibility to investigate fraud, to give policy advice (5 U.S.C. § 404; IG Act, sec. 4), to handle certain complaints by employees, and to report to the heads of their agencies and to Congress on their activities every six months (5 U.S.C. § 405; IG Act, sec. 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates substantive functions: document review, fraud investigations, policy advice, handling employee complaints, and semiannual reporting to agency heads and Congress. Also implies authority to issue subpoenas during audits/investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural reorganization of existing oversight offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Many existing offices with names like Office of Audit, Office of Investigations, or similar were transferred, renamed, folded into the new IG offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act required consolidation/transfer of preexisting audit/investigation units into the newly established OIGs — a structural/organizational requirement affecting where responsibilities reside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General Reform Act of 2008 — creation of CIGIE
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act and the Inspector General role were amended thirty years later by the Inspector General Reform Act of 2008, which created the umbrella IG agency, Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes an inter-office council to coordinate integrity and efficiency efforts across OIGs; reflects an institutional standard for oversight coordination and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing Inspector General Independence Act of 2022 — congressional notice and removal protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress must be informed by the president 30 days in advance notice before removing any inspector general and given "the substantive rationale, including detailed and case-specific reasons" for doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates procedural protections around IG removal designed to increase transparency and constrain arbitrary dismissals. This is a statutory standard governing executive actions affecting IG tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing Inspector General Independence Act of 2022 — expanded protections and vacancy rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Securing Inspector General Independence Act of 2022 amended Inspector General Act of 1978 to expand protections for Inspectors General being removed, transferred or placed on non-duty status, limited who may fill the role of Acting Inspector General in the event of a vacancy, and required Acting IGs to report to Congress regarding ongoing OIG investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets limits on appointing acting IGs (to preserve independence) and requires reporting by Acting IGs about ongoing investigations, thereby maintaining continuity and accountability during vacancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing Inspector General Independence Act of 2022 — reporting, notification, and cooperation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The act streamlined existing requirements for OIG Semiannual Reports to Congress, required IGs to report Congress when information or assistance is unreasonably refused or not provided by the Department, and required that non-governmental organizations and business entities be notified and provided an opportunity to comment on non-investigative OIG reports in which they are specifically identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes procedural obligations on OIGs and departments: (1) semiannual reporting rules were adjusted; (2) OIGs must notify Congress if departments unreasonably withhold information/assistance; (3) non-governmental entities identified in non‑investigative reports must receive notice and an opportunity to comment — a fairness/notice requirement for reporting practice.
